title: Seabright Utilities on‑prem resiliency playbook and Terraform module notes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures proposed sizing, resiliency assumptions, Terraform module organization, and an upgrade/rollback playbook for the Seabright Utilities private deployment (edge sites + central control plane). It is a working draft intended for the Solutions Engineering handoff, SRE review, and customer architecture approval.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Single-region on‑prem deployment footprint for Seabright (three datacenter racks: control plane, inference pool, shared infra).
- Network/VPC topology, perf and failover assumptions, KMS/HSM integration notes.
- Terraform module breakdown and state management recommendations.
- Planned upgrade strategy, rollback steps, and test/acceptance criteria.
- Open questions to resolve before cutover.

High level architecture summary (customer constraints):
- Seabright requires air-gapped-capable deployment with egress-restricted control plane and optional periodic sync windows for model updates.
- Expected steady state: 120 peak concurrent inference sessions, median request size ~250 tokens, 95th percentile latency SLO: 350ms for streaming generation turn (~single-turn user prompt).
- Preferred GPU hardware on customer racks: A10G / A30 for cost‑sensitive inference pools; reserve 1–2 H100 nodes for heavy batch/quantization validation tasks during rollout.

Sizing assumptions and capacity math (ballpark):
- Baseline QPS estimate: 20–40 requests/sec (concurrent sessions 120 translates to ~1–2 QPS if sessions are long; we size for token throughput).
- Model: medium‑sized decoder-only models in the 7–13B family (FP16 or 4-bit quant profiles).
- Per-node capacity estimate: A10G node (48GB) supports ~20 concurrent low-latency single-turn streams for 13B quantized model (highly workload dependent).
- Recommended initial pool: 6x A10G inference nodes + 2x control-plane instances (4 vCPU, 16GB) + 1x HSM/KMS gateway appliance. Reserve 30% headroom for bursts.
- Storage: model cache NVMe per GPU node, 2TB per node (models cached on local disk for fast startup).

Networking and L2/L3 considerations:
- VPC/Overlay: customer to provide a dedicated VPC or VLAN with /22 addressing for the deployment. Control plane and inference nodes split into subnets with route filtering between management and inference networks.
- Service mesh is optional; initial deployment uses direct routing with egress-firewall rules for model sync windows.
- MTU and jumbo frames: require validation. If using RDMA for GPU nodes, ensure 9000 MTU across the fabric.
- Peering/failover: plan for single peering to the central support network; define fallback to a secondary link (MPLS or LTE) for control-plane telemetry only.

Security, KMS and HSM notes:
- KMS: integrate with customer KMS (Vault or cloud KMS exposed via gateway). Terraform modules will support either: external KMS endpoint or local HSM client (PKCS11).
- Secrets: avoid storing unencrypted keys in Terraform state. Use remote secret injection via Vault agent or HashiCorp boundary for runtime secrets.
- Audit: enable verbose audit logs for key operations, store logs in central SIEM via secure forwarder.

Terraform module design (recommendation):
- Module layout (separate modules, each tested independently):
  - network-vpc (subnets, routes, firewall rules)
  - infra-base (control-plane instance configs, load balancers)
  - gpu-pool (node group provisioning, NVMe setup, driver install hooks)
  - secrets-integration (placeholders for Vault / KMS wiring)
  - monitoring-observability (prometheus rules, grafana dashboards, alerting)
  - tf-state (lock + backend config templates)
- State backend: Customer to provide S3-compatible object store + Dynamo/consul for locks. Default environment example: s3://seabright-terraform-state (lock via dynamodb). For air-gapped, use on‑prem MinIO + Consul; document DR for state store.
- Module variables: prefer small, explicit set. Example variables to expose: instance_type, gpu_count_per_node, model_cache_path, kms_endpoint, allowed_control_ips, enable_rdma(bool).
- Outputs: node_ips, control_plane_lb, monitoring_endpoints, kms_status. Keep outputs minimal and avoid secrets in outputs.
- Versioning: tag all modules and reference via registry module source or pinned git tags. Keep breaking changes behind major version increments.

Provisioning hooks and bootstrap (operational notes):
- Use Ansible/Chef for GPU driver + container runtime installation post-provisioning; Terraform handles infra only. Keep driver installers in an internal artifact repo.
- Bootstrap sequence: network -> tf-state -> infra-base -> gpu-pool -> secrets-integration -> monitoring.
- Model sync: scheduled sync using controlled windows. Models are verified by checksum before being loaded into node caches.

Upgrade and rollout plan (high level):
- Canary first: add a single canary node (same instance type) to the gpu-pool with traffic routed to it via a small canary weight (5%). Run automated correctness checks and perf tests for a minimum of 4 hours.
- Phased rollout: 20% -> 50% -> 100% across pools, with automated health gates (token latency, p50/p95, error rate, cost delta).
- Fallback policy: if any gate triggers, automatically route to previous model variant or smaller model family. Maintain at least 2 warmed fallback nodes.

Rollback playbook (step-by-step):
1) Detect: alert triggers (latency spike, error > 1% rolling, increased memory OOM).
2) Quarantine new nodes: mark canary nodes as unschedulable for new sessions (drain existing requests).
3) Switch routing: update load balancer / router to route to previous stable pool.
4) Evict and reprovision: drain and reprovision canary nodes using previous stable AMI/config.
5) Postmortem: collect debug bundles from failed nodes (cpu/gpu metrics, kernel logs, container logs), open JIRA, triage.

Acceptance criteria (customer signoff):
- Functional: baseline queries pass the correctness test suite (100 sample prompts verified).
- Performance: median latency <= 250ms, p95 <= 350ms, error rate < 0.5% for steady workload during acceptance window (24 hours simulated traffic).
- Resiliency: single GPU node failure does not increase error rate above 1% and recovery < 10 minutes (automated reprovisioning).
- Security: KMS integration validated with remote key unwrap and audit log capture.

Observability and SLOs:
- Required dashboards: token-level throughput, node-level GPU utilization, kv-cache hit rate, request latency (p50/p95/p99), model load times.
- Alerting thresholds to define: gpu_utilization>95% for 10m, sustained p95 latency degradation >20%, model-load failures > 2 per hour.

Open questions / decisions (needs customer input):
- Preferred GPU SKUs for initial buy vs. scale—A10G vs. A30 vs. H100 (budget + thermal capacity constraints).
- KMS vendor: will customer provide PKCS11-compatible HSM or a Vault gateway?
- State backend preference in air‑gapped mode (MinIO+Consul vs. local NFS locks).
- Acceptable maintenance window frequency for model syncs (weekly vs. biweekly).

Operational runbook snippets (commands & checks):
- Health check: curl -sS http://control-plane.local/healthz | jq .
- GPU health: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 5
- Terraform plan/validate: terraform init -backend-config="bucket=seabright-terraform-state" && terraform plan -var-file=env.yaml

Handover checklist for solutions engineering -> SRE: (minimal)
- Confirm rack-level power and cooling constraints for GPU nodes.
- Confirm network MTU/RDMA requirements.
- Provide KMS/HSM endpoint and test credentials.
- Finalize Terraform state backend and locking mechanism.
- Provide access to artifact repo for driver installers and model checksums.

Next steps (near term):
- Resolve open questions with Seabright infra lead (schedule decision meeting week of 2024-11-18).
- Prototype a single-node canary in customer lab using A10G (target week 2024-12-02).
- Create GH PR template for module updates with required perf regression checks (owner: Samira).

Appendix: quick links and references
- Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood/example/seabright-onprem-reqs
- Jira epic: JIRA-1427 (Seabright onprem delivery)
- GitHub infra repo PR: GH-PR-2981

Notes: this doc is intentionally conversational and contains rough numbers for planning. Final sizing will come from a short performance runbook performed on-customer-hardware with representative prompt traffic (we will run the Redwood perf harness and capture token throughput curves).
